Sonia —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary we typically provide in a bid response; I have attached a short evidence pack and a regression playbook (summary). Happy to expand any section for committee review.

1) NIST AI RMF mapping (summary):
- Identify: Model inventory + versioning (automated catalog with model hashes and provenance metadata); risk tiering by use case and data sensitivity; threat modeling for integrations.
- Protect: Hardened serving runtime with per-customer key management (KMS), network segmentation (for Private), and role-based access controls mapped to least privilege.
- Detect: Continuous telemetry (per-route latency/error metrics), model output drift detection (embedding drift + output distribution tests), and anomalous request pattern alerts.
- Respond: Out-of-band incident runbooks, automated model rollback (pinned stable variant), and canary isolation for suspected regressions.
- Recover: Immutable audit logs, snapshot restore of model-serving state, and documented continuity procedures.

2) EU AI Act — conformity & artifacts:
- Standard deliverable: traceability logs for served model inputs/outputs (configurable retention), model version manifest, model card (capabilities and intended use), and a summary of evaluation results for provided benchmark prompt sets.
- Add-on services: full training-data provenance reports, access to raw eval artifacts, extended retention of request/response logs for auditors, and on-site evidence review sessions.
- We support packaging these artifacts for conformity assessment bodies (we provide templates used by prior customers).

3) Regression testing & customer tooling integration:
- Cadence: baseline public-eval and internal regression suite run at each model/version release. For production customers we recommend weekly regression runs plus triggered runs on rollout.
- Tooling: Redwood Optimize provides exportable regression artifacts (seeded prompt sets, expected responses, metrics) and a Jenkins-friendly CLI for automated runs. We also provide a Dockerized evaluation harness compatible with privacy-preserving synthetic data pipelines.
- Integration options: webhooks on regression failures, REST API to kick off customer-side evals, and a reproducible eval bundle (JSON prompts + expected outputs + scoring script) you can run inside your CI.

Attached: RFI_Response_Summary.pdf (2pg), SOC2_Snapshot.pdf (security snapshot), Regression_Playbook_v1.xlsx (cadence + example tests).
